body:
m1 cross-review of W3 correction a15396e (chief-assigned): ACCEPT - no REQUIRED findings, two nits. I ran this one myself in the main session: three fresh-context reviewer agents were killed in a row by account limits, so this is a hand-run pass in a clean worktree at the SHA (pin 0329c43), 31 adversarial probes (mine plus the ones the last killed agent had already written), JVM and Scala.js.

ENFORCEMENT (the HIGH is closed). validateTransformation recomputes the detector's own matches and requires each mapped destination slice to equal that entry's configured pseudonym. Probes, all refused as they should be: UNLISTED-SECRET; [REDACTED]X (superset); [REDACTE] (truncated); [redacted] (case variant); another entry's pseudonym; the shorter entry's pseudonym on a longest-whole-word winner (Ann / Anne / Mary Ann); swapped pseudonyms across two occurrences; a second occurrence with a different replacement; a case-insensitive entry given a case-variant of its own pseudonym; a pseudonym that is itself another entry's surface (also caught by destination re-detection); altered gap text outside mapped spans. Exact configured pseudonyms certify. No raw surface, pseudonym, or destination string appears in any Left, in PseudonymizationDetector.toString, or in PseudonymizationTableEntry.toString - canary-grepped.

CANONICAL INDEX: identity and the reported entry index are invariant over all 6 permutations of a 3-row table; duplicate rows and NFC/NFD rows behave as distinct configured surfaces (no silent Unicode unification).

ORDERING (the part I looked hardest at, since the check is a positional zip): sound today because detectTable is exactly detectTableMatches(...).map(_.span), and checked asserts sourceDetection.spans == offsets.map(_._1) at :511-518 before calling validateTransformation, so matches and offsets are in the same order by construction. The new final sort key (matched.entryIndex) only makes an existing stable order explicit.

UNCHANGED MATCHING: the boundary predicates (isWordCodePoint, boundaryBefore/After, regionMatches) are untouched by the diff; the only sort-key change is the added entryIndex tiebreak. So the whole-word behaviour at 9f6b0f8 is preserved.

CROSS-PLATFORM: all 31 probes pass IDENTICALLY on JVM and Scala.js, including combining marks, CJK neighbours, Deseret supplementary code points in both the surface and the neighbour position, apostrophe and hyphen boundaries, NFC vs NFD, and Turkish dotted capital I. This matters because the ADR claims equal detector identity implies equal behaviour, and the matcher goes through java.lang.Character - on the probed inputs that claim holds on both platforms.

COUNTS at a15396e (clean pin): embedCoreJVM 134/134 and embedCoreJS 134/134 (103 committed + 31 probes), interviewJVM 41/41. scalafmtCheckAll not re-run (my probe files are the only would-be offenders; the author's exact-SHA run was green).

NIT 1 (defense in depth): validateTransformation is private[embed] and its positional zip is correct only because of a precondition asserted by its single caller. A future embed-core caller could pass offsets in another order and get pairwise comparisons against the wrong entries. One line inside the zip - also require matched.span == the offset's source span, else the same InvariantViolation - makes the invariant local instead of caller-dependent.
NIT 2 (documentation): under caseInsensitive, Turkish dotted capital I folds onto ASCII i, so a table row "ismail" detects "ISMAIL" spelled with U+0130. That direction is fail-safe (over-detection means more redaction, and destination re-detection gets stricter, never laxer), but since detector identity is supposed to fix behaviour, the folding rule deserves a sentence in the Scaladoc next to the whole-word rule.

Both nits are follow-ups, not landing blockers. codex-storymodel-new-engineer: nothing to redo. Chief: from my side a15396e is ready to land, and the scout's cf162a9 can then rebase onto it as the ordered pair you sequenced.
